defects.description: _mode_args raises a plain ValueError for an unknown mode, while every other validation in this section (and the module) raises ExaError. The ExaError docstring explicitly covers 'an invalid option combo is given', so a caller doing `except ExaError` around search()/run() will NOT catch a bad mode and will get an unhandled ValueError instead.
defects.suggestion: Raise ExaError (or a dedicated subclass) for unknown mode to match the rest of the module.

defects.description: search(stream=True) sets body['stream']=True, but the transport _request() always parses a single JSON body via resp.json() (line 510) and never consumes an SSE stream. The parameter is therefore a no-op that cannot deliver a stream; the real streaming path is the separate stream_search() at line 2807. Advertsing `stream` on search() is misleading.
defects.suggestion: Remove the `stream` parameter from search() or route it to the streaming transport; it currently cannot work.

defects.description: In _contents_block, include_html_tags, include_sections and exclude_sections are emitted only inside the text sub-dict (lines 1360-1365), which is only reached when `with_text or max_characters or text_verbosity` is truthy. If a caller sets only e.g. include_sections=[...] with no text option, the entire block is skipped and the parameter is silently ignored with no error.
defects.suggestion: Either reject these section/HTML options when no text is requested, or at least warn; don't silently drop them.

defects.description: livecrawl is annotated Optional[str] in search() (and defaults to False in _contents_block at line 1340), but the Exa contents field is a boolean and is emitted verbatim via `if livecrawl: c['livecrawl'] = livecrawl` (line 1405). Passing a string would send a string where the API expects a bool.
defects.suggestion: Type it as Optional[bool] and normalize to bool before emitting.

defects.description: _category_canon prints a warning to stdout and returns None for an unsupported category, so the user's requested category filter is silently not applied and search() runs without it. For a library this means stdout output on a data path and results that differ from what was requested, with no exception.
defects.suggestion: Consider raising or returning a sentinel that lets search() decide; stdout-print from a helper is a code smell and the filter drop is easy to miss.

    timeout: float = 90.0,

functions.purpose: POST a natural-language query to /answer and wrap the response in an Answer.
functions.notes: Always parses a single JSON body via _request; the stream=True path is not handled (see defects).

defects.description: answer() accepts and forwards an undocumented `stream` parameter (declared line 1900, not in the Args docstring) into body["stream"] (line 1939), but routes through _request() which does resp.json(). When stream=True the /answer endpoint returns an SSE stream (as stream_answer at line 2642 confirms by posting stream=True and parsing SSE lines), so resp.json() raises an uncaught httpx/JSON decode error instead of returning an Answer. Passing stream=True to answer() crashes with an obscure error; the documented streaming path is stream_answer().
defects.suggestion: Either document/validate stream (raise a clear error directing the user to stream_answer when stream=True) or parse the SSE stream; simplest is to reject stream=True with an ExaError pointing to stream_answer().

defects.description: The legacy string-form guard checks only `not extras_links and max_age_hours is None` (line 1824), ignoring the other rich extras (extras_image_links, extras_rich_links, extras_rich_image_links, extras_code_blocks) and other rich options (text_verbosity, subpages, include_sections, highlights_max_characters). So a single-URL text fetch such as fetch(urls=[u], extras_code_blocks=5) still returns the plain '--- Title ---\n<body>' string and silently discards the requested structured extras, contradicting the docstring promise that the string form is used only 'when no rich options are requested'.
defects.suggestion: Make the guard cover all rich options (any extras_*, text_verbosity, subpages>0, subpage_target, include_sections, etc.) so the structured list is returned whenever a rich option is actually requested.

defects.description: Answer.__init__ sets self.citations = raw.get("citations", []) (line 1854). If the /answer API returns the key with a null value ("citations": null) the default is not applied, so citations becomes None; Answer.sources (line 1860), to_dict (line 1866), to_markdown (line 1879) and __repr__ (line 1891) then raise TypeError ('NoneType' not iterable / not a len()). The sibling stream_answer defensively normalizes with `obj.get("citations") or []` (line 2672), confirming empty/absent citations is a real response shape, so Answer should use the same guard.
defects.suggestion: Use self.citations = raw.get("citations") or [] to mirror stream_answer and avoid the None crash.

defects.description: Answer.to_markdown renders the answer body with str(self.answer) (line 1877). When output_schema is supplied, self.answer is a dict, and str() emits Python repr (single-quoted, non-JSON) rather than valid JSON, so the '## Answer' block is not a clean structured payload.
defects.suggestion: Serialize a dict answer with json.dumps(answer, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) instead of str() when the answer is not a string.

defects.description: agent() early-returns a terminal run created already terminal (`if run.done: return run`) without running the `raise_on_failed` check at line 2425. If POST /agent/runs returns a run that is already `failed` (rare per the comment, but e.g. an instantly-failing continuation), the default `raise_on_failed=True` contract documented in the docstring (lines 2368-2369, 2375-2377) is violated: a failed AgentRun is silently returned instead of raising ExaError, unlike the poll path which does raise.
defects.suggestion: Move/apply the `if raise_on_failed and run.status == "failed": raise` check after the early return as well (check both the pre-poll and post-poll run objects).

defects.description: The docstring says `timeout` is the 'Max total wall-clock seconds to wait for completion' (line 2366), but `deadline = time.time() + timeout` is computed AFTER the create call at line 2404, which itself runs with `timeout=min(timeout, 30)`; each in-flight poll GET at line 2412 also carries `timeout=min(timeout, 45)`. Total elapsed wall-clock can therefore exceed `timeout` by up to ~30s (create) + up to ~45s (one in-flight poll) for default timeout=120, and for small timeouts (e.g. timeout=10) the actual wait can be roughly double the promised bound.
defects.suggestion: Subtract elapsed time from the create call before computing the deadline (e.g. record t0 before POST and use `deadline = t0 + timeout`), and/or cap the per-poll request timeout by remaining time.

defects.description: agent_trace() wraps json.loads of a string event `data` in `try/except: pass` (lines 2317-2321), so if the API ever returns a string payload that is not valid JSON the field stays a str. AgentTrace._parse then calls `data.get(...)` on that str (e.g. line 2129 `item = data.get("item") or {}`), raising AttributeError 'str' object has no attribute 'get' and crashing agent_trace entirely.
defects.suggestion: On parse failure, drop the event or set e["data"] = {} instead of leaving the raw string, or make AgentTrace._parse tolerate non-dict `data` (guard with isinstance(d, dict)).

defects.description: AgentRun.citations iterates `for c in g.get("citations", [])`; the default only covers a missing key. If the API sends a grounding group with `"citations": null`, iterating None raises TypeError. The sibling code in this file consistently defends with `or []` (e.g. AgentRun.__init__ line 1967, AgentTrace._parse lines 2129/2142), so a null here is handled less defensively than the rest of the module.
defects.suggestion: Use `for c in (g.get("citations") or []):`.

defects.description: _run_fallback (line 1059) returns None for ANY failure of the fallback endpoint (connection error, non-200, non-JSON), and _request returns that None at line 1044 as if it were a successful payload. The sole caller _search_full (line 2010) immediately executes `diag = _query_diag(data)` and `data.get(...)` with data=None, raising AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get' at line 2011. Trigger: mode='local' with a key lacking local support that returns a retryable status (429/5xx/404) on the local endpoint while the web fallback GET also fails. The docs promise 'Local mode can fall back to web search; inspect `fallback`' (references/api.md line 96) — instead the whole search crashes.
defects.suggestion: In _request, when `fallback` is set and `_run_fallback` returns None, raise the original classified error (`error`) instead of returning None.

defects.description: `if isinstance(data, dict) or data is not None:` is a tautology equivalent to `if data is not None:` (a dict is never None). So the intended '200-but-unparseable is a server-side oddity; treat as transient' path (lines 1017-1025) is unreachable: resp.json() that parses to None (literal 'null'), a bare JSON string, number, or list is returned as the payload. Any downstream `data.get(...)` (e.g. _query_diag at line 1716) then crashes with AttributeError/TypeError on a non-dict 'successful' response.
defects.suggestion: Use `if isinstance(data, dict):` so non-dict/None 200 bodies fall through to the retry/raise path as the comment intends.

defects.description: `if fallback and resp.status_code != 200 and (retryable or not fast_fail and fallback is not None):` — `and` binds tighter than `or`, so the condition is `... and (retryable or ((not fast_fail) and (fallback is not None)))`. `fallback is not None` is always true here (first clause of the chain), making the inner `and` dead; and a fast-fail status that is also retryable (e.g. a 429 body tagged component=authentication) silently takes the fallback, inverting the 'definitive errors are not retried/fallen-back' contract stated in the docstring (lines 975-976).
defects.suggestion: Explicitly parenthesise: `if fallback and resp.status_code != 200 and (retryable or not fast_fail):` and drop the redundant `fallback is not None` (and possibly the _fallback_ok stub).

defects.description: fast_fail treats VALIDATION as definitive only when `resp.status_code == 422 and code == 'VALIDATION'`, whereas _classify_response (line 857) classifies `code == 'VALIDATION'` as 'param' regardless of status. A 400/500 response whose body carries error.code='VALIDATION' therefore gets retried by _request (fast_fail False) and, after retries, raised with category='param' even though the real failure was a non-validation HTTP error — callers reacting on .category get the wrong verdict.
defects.suggestion: Align the two: have _request compute fast_fail via the same predicate as _classify_response, or drop the status guard in _classify_response.

defects.description: In _classify_response, if the meta.errors normalisation comprehension raises (e.g. an entry whose 'loc' is a non-iterable non-string), `except Exception: pass` leaves `details` as the RAW unnormalized list (still set from line 859). The caller then reports un-normalised details and str()s the raw list in the 200-char message instead of falling back to the body text.
defects.suggestion: Set `details = None` (or a sentinel) in the except block so the fallback message uses the raw body.

defects.description: _read_key_file accepts ANY line with length >= 12 and no '/' as the API key (`elif len(line) >= 12 and "/" not in line and line not in names: return line...`). For a file like ~/.prime/agent/keys/secrets.env that also defines BRAVE_API_KEY, the first 12+ char line that isn't KEY=VALUE for a Brave name (a comment without '#', a shebang, another service's bare token) is returned as the Brave key before the real BRAVE_API_KEY= line is ever seen — wrong credential silently used.
defects.suggestion: Only return bare-line values from files dedicated to this key (the stem.key / names.lower().key files); require KEY=VALUE form for generic .env files.

defects.description: `elif code == "VALIDATION" or status == 422 and meta.get("errors"):` parses as `code == 'VALIDATION' or (status == 422 and meta.get('errors'))` due to precedence; works by luck but any 4xx/5xx body containing error.code='VALIDATION' is classified 'param' with meta.errors possibly empty/None, even though the transport error is the real issue. Add parentheses for clarity.
defects.suggestion: elif code == "VALIDATION" or (status == 422 and meta.get("errors")):

defects.description: `try: from dotenv import dotenv_values ... except Exception: pass` wraps the entire dotenv loop, but only an ImportError can occur before the loop body; any unexpected error from dotenv_values() (corrupt/oversized .env) is silently swallowed, so a misconfigured dotenv file yields no signal and the search later fails with the generic 'no API key' message.
defects.suggestion: Catch only ImportError around the import; let dotenv_values errors surface or log them.

defects.description: BraveError docstring lists `timeout` and `http_422` as valid categories, but grep confirms neither string is ever assigned anywhere in the module. Callers checking `category == 'timeout'` (or distinguishing http_422 from param) can never match; timeouts surface as category='network' instead.
defects.suggestion: Either assign these categories where timeouts/422s are handled, or remove them from the docstring.

defects.description: The `timeout` parameter of _classify_response is never referenced in the body; it is threaded from _request (lines 1046/1047) purely for symmetry.
defects.suggestion: Drop the parameter or use it in the message (e.g. note the timeout value on network-related classifications).

defects.description: The error message embeds `str(details if details else body)[:200]` — up to 200 chars of the raw response body (or raw details list repr) into an exception message. If a response body ever echoes the X-Subscription-Token or other credential material, it would leak into logs/agent transcripts.
defects.suggestion: Limit the embedded body to a fixed set of safe fields (error.code/error.detail) rather than raw body text.

defects.description: _fallback_ok is a trivial `return bool(fallback)` stub invoked only from _request line 1042 where the enclosing `if fallback and ...` already guarantees truthiness; it adds an indirection with no decision.
defects.suggestion: Inline the check (or remove both) and let _request call _run_fallback directly.

defects.description: _get_api_key backfills the resolved key into os.environ for ALL _API_KEY_NAMES via setdefault — a side effect beyond the documented lookup, mutating process-wide state for sibling threads/imports and non-thread-safe with concurrent first calls (two threads can both miss the cache and race the setdefault; harmless result-wise since values agree, but the env mutation is observable).
defects.suggestion: Document the env backfill explicitly or drop it; guard the cache read/write if true concurrency on first use is expected.

defects.description: The deprecation gate regex r"\b(deprecat|obsolete|removed|migrat|breaking|sunset)\b" (also 5800, and the shaded copies 5550/5554/5567) requires a word boundary on BOTH sides of each stem. Since 'deprecat', 'remov', 'migrat' are stems, not whole words, \bdeprecat\b only matches the literal non-word 'deprecat'. Verified: it fails to match 'deprecated', 'deprecation', 'deprecating', 'removed', 'removal', 'migration', 'migrating' — i.e. the actual deprecation vocabulary — while only catching whole words 'obsolete', 'removed', 'breaking', 'sunset', 'end of life'. _dep_type() (substring, no \b) would classify 'deprecated' fine, but items never reach it because this gate rejects them first. Net effect: deprecations() returns near-empty signals/counts for its primary use case.
defects.suggestion: Drop the trailing \b (keep leading \b only) or use substring matching: r"\b(deprecat|obsolet|end[- ]of[- ]life|remov|migrat|breaking|sunset)" so stems match as prefixes.

defects.description: is_deprecated() derives its entire 'deprecated' verdict from deprecations(...).get('signals') (line 5915-5917). Because deprecations() is neutered by the broken \b regex gate, signals is almost always empty, so is_deprecated() returns {'deprecated': False} even for genuinely deprecated packages. The freshness/news check (active_recent) does not feed the verdict, so the advertised deprecation-detection capability silently does not work.

defects.description: The ThreadPoolExecutor is a process-lifetime singleton sized by the FIRST call to _pool/_fanout. A later _fanout(jobs, concurrency=N) with N > the initial size silently runs on the smaller pool, and max(8, ...) forces at least 8 in-flight jobs even when the caller explicitly passes a smaller concurrency (e.g. concurrency=2 to stay under a rate limit still submits with 8 running). The `concurrency` parameter therefore does not reliably bound parallelism.
defects.suggestion: Create/resize the pool when requested max_workers exceeds the current pool size (or document that the first call's concurrency is fixed for the process and honor a lower bound instead of max(8, ...)).

defects.description: Only `except Exception` is caught around fut.result() (line 77); a BaseException raised by a job (SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt) propagates out of _fanout, aborting collection of the remaining already-submitted futures and returning no result at all. Also, if a thunk is not callable, pool.submit raises TypeError mid-loop after earlier futures are already queued, leaving them orphaned and no partial results.
defects.suggestion: Catch BaseException per future (or validate thunks up front and catch submit errors per job) so one bad job cannot discard the whole fanout.

defects.description: _http (lines 33-35) and _pool (lines 44-46) use unsynchronized check-then-set lazy initialization of the module globals _CLIENT/_WORKERS; two threads racing on first use can each construct a client/pool, and the loser is abandoned (its connections never closed promptly). The _http docstring claims the client is thread-safe but the creation path itself is not atomic.
defects.suggestion: Guard creation with a module-level lock (or accept the benign race explicitly in the docstring).

defects.description: resp.headers is httpx's case-insensitive headers dict, so resp.headers.get("retry-after") (second operand of the `or`) can never find a header the first .get("Retry-After") missed; the second lookup is a no-op fallback that never adds anything.

defects.description: _get_api_key returns _API_KEY_CACHE[label] before ever re-reading the environment. Once a key has been resolved, a corrected EXA_API_KEY re-exported in the same long-lived process (exactly the recovery the ExaAuthError message on line 528 tells the user to do: 'export a fresh EXA_API_KEY') is ignored and the stale key keeps producing 401s forever. There is no cache-invalidation or re-check path anywhere in the module.
defects.suggestion: Prefer the live environment variable over the cache (cache only file-derived keys, or re-run _seek_api_key when os.environ.get(_API_KEY_NAMES[0]) differs from the cached value).

defects.description: Missing key raises a bare RuntimeError, but the ExaAuthError docstring (lines 382-383) says it covers 'the API key is missing, invalid, or revoked' and references/usage.md tells users to catch ExaAuthError for auth problems. Callers following the docs and catching ExaAuthError will miss the missing-key case entirely.
defects.suggestion: Raise ExaAuthError (or document RuntimeError explicitly) for the not-configured case so the documented catch set works.

defects.description: _read_key_file's bare-token branch returns the first line with no '=', length >= 12 and no '/' as the key without checking it belongs to any name in `names`. In a key/env file whose first qualifying token is not the Exa key (e.g. a comment-free header token, a date-like string, or another service's token in secrets.env), the wrong value is silently returned as the API key, surfacing later only as a confusing 401.
defects.suggestion: For files that contain '='-style lines, require NAME= matches; only accept a bare token when the file contains no assignment lines at all (or name it <stem>.key explicitly).

defects.description: Bare 'except Exception: pass' around the dotenv import + value loop swallows all errors (unreadable/permission-denied dotenv files, parser bugs) and falls through to key-file lookup with no trace; the fallback chain then returns '' or a wrong-source key without indicating the dotenv step failed.
defects.suggestion: Catch only ImportError for the missing optional dependency; let per-file read errors raise or at least be distinguishable.

defects.description: 'return resp.json()' on any status < 400 is unguarded: a 2xx response with an empty or non-JSON body raises ValueError/json.JSONDecodeError out of _request, which the module's documented error contract (Exa* subclasses from ExaError) does not cover.
defects.suggestion: Wrap resp.json() in try/except and raise a wrapped ExaServerError with the status code and a snippet of resp.text.

defects.description: Lines 552-553 ('# unreachable' / final raise) are unreachable for any _retries >= 0: every loop path either returns (<400) or raises. Additionally 'last_resp' (assigned lines 504 and 511) is never read, and 'detail' would be None in the dead fallback message.
defects.suggestion: Remove the unreachable fallback and the unused last_resp assignment, or convert _retries to assert max(0, _retries) and use last_resp for the diagnostic.

defects.description: Redundant 'import time' inside _request; time is already imported at module level (line 12) and used by _retry_after_seconds at module scope.
defects.suggestion: Drop the local import.

defects.description: __version__ = '0.19.0' is stale: pyproject.toml declares version = '0.20.0' (and the package was imported as v0.20.0 in commit d5e521f), so programmatic version checks disagree with the installed/packaged version.

defects.description: stream_answer's docstring documents the trailing meta dict as "cost_dollars": {...} (an object), and the rest of the module treats cost as a dict (e.g. costDollars.total, SearchResults.total_cost). But the code (line 2675) collapses it to the scalar float (obj.get('costDollars') or {}).get('total'), so the yielded dict actually carries cost_dollars as a float/None.

defects.description: stream_search (and stream_answer at 2659) parse exactly one JSON object per 'data:' SSE line and, on json failure, `continue` (drop the frame). The sibling stream_answer_source handles this correctly with a frame_buffer (2766-2783).
defects.suggestion: Buffer consecutive 'data:' lines and join with '\n' before json.loads, as stream_answer_source does, rather than parsing line-by-line.

defects.description: stream_search's Yields docstring (2823-2824) lists the final dict as {results, output, grounding, citations, text, request_id}, but the actual final yield (2907-2915) also includes search_time_ms (captured at 2858/2880). defects.description: _fanout's `concurrency` argument does not control actual in-flight concurrency. It only feeds `_pool(max(8, concurrency))`, and _pool creates the executor exactly once (first call wins); _WORKERS is never resized. So the pool's worker count is fixed by whichever call first touched it (typically the 8-worker default), and every later _fanout(concurrency=2/3/4/16) silently reuses that same pool. The documented `batch(concurrency=...)` 'max in-flight requests' knob and the mode-specific limits (mosaic=3, rich=2, paged=4) are effectively no-ops: all jobs queue to the same fixed-size pool.
defects.suggestion: Create a dedicated bounded executor per concurrency value, or use a semaphore to actually cap in-flight jobs, or drop the parameter so it isn't misleading.

defects.description: _norm_url lowercases the ENTIRE URL (scheme+host+path+query) and returns u.lower(). URL paths and query values are case-sensitive per RFC 3986, so two distinct results whose paths differ only by case (e.g. /Page vs /page, /Apple vs /apple) are treated as the same identity. This silently drops legitimately-distinct hits in _dedupe_hits and can over-suppress the image/page/website 'same URL' checks in _slim_item/_slim_infobox.
defects.suggestion: Lowercase only the scheme and host; preserve case in the path and query string.

defects.description: For a timestamped date, _one_date returns `s.replace("Z", "").split(".")[0]`, stripping the trailing 'Z' (UTC marker). The resulting string (e.g. '2025-01-15T10:30:00') is a naive ISO string with no timezone; consumers that parse it (Python <=3.10 fromisoformat, or downstream code) treat it as wall-clock/local time, shifting the real UTC instant by the viewer's offset. The stripping appears aimed at py3.10 fromisoformat not accepting 'Z', but it silently discards timezone information from the 'date' field the agent view exposes.
defects.suggestion: Preserve the timezone (e.g. keep 'Z' or convert to an explicit offset) rather than emitting a naive string, or document that 'date' is UTC-naive.

defects.description: _AsyncBool subclasses int, not bool. isinstance(result, bool) is False and json.dumps serializes it as 1/0 rather than true/false. This only matters if a public function returns a bare bool (none currently do in this section, so it is latent), but it means the 'awaitable bool' is not a real bool to callers using type checks or JSON round-trips.
defects.suggestion: Subclass bool, or handle bools by returning a wrapper whose __await__ and JSON behaviour are unambiguous.

defects.description: _http() and _pool() use an unsynchronized check-then-set on the module globals _CLIENT/_WORKERS. Under the fanout thread pool the first concurrent use can race and construct two clients / two executors, leaking one. httpx.Client.request is thread-safe, but the lazy init itself is not.
defects.suggestion: Guard the one-time init with a module-level lock (or use a module-scope `if _CLIENT is None: _CLIENT = ...` plus a lock / threading.local) so only one instance is created.

defects.description: The dual sync/async docstring (lines 511-512) promises that 'the module's own container classes (SearchResults, Answer, ...) get an __await__ that returns the instance unchanged', and _identity_await is defined for exactly that purpose. But no such container class exists in the module (the only classes are the _Async* wrappers and BraveError) and _identity_await is never assigned to any class, so it is dead code and the documented mechanism is not actually present.
defects.suggestion: Remove _identity_await and the 'container classes get __await__' claim, or add the container classes if they are intended.

all_defects.description: _run_fallback (line 1059) returns None for ANY failure of the fallback endpoint (connection error, non-200, non-JSON), and _request returns that None at line 1044 as if it were a successful payload. The sole caller _search_full (line 2010) immediately executes `diag = _query_diag(data)` and `data.get(...)` with data=None, raising AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get' at line 2011. Trigger: mode='local' with a key lacking local support that returns a retryable status (429/5xx/404) on the local endpoint while the web fallback GET also fails. The docs promise 'Local mode can fall back to web search; inspect `fallback`' (references/api.md line 96) — instead the whole search crashes.
all_defects.suggestion: In _request, when `fallback` is set and `_run_fallback` returns None, raise the original classified error (`error`) instead of returning None.

all_defects.description: _summarizer fallback path builds a malformed deep link: 'https://search.brave.com/summarizer?key=' + _up.urlencode({'key': key}) produces '...summarizer?key=key=%3C...%3E' (the literal 'key=' prefix is doubled because urlencode already emits the key name). The success path at line 1776 correctly uses '?' + urlencode without the hardcoded 'key='. Any string key that fails json.loads (or parses to a non-dict, e.g. a string, triggering AttributeError at line 1769) hits this branch and yields a broken link.

all_defects.description: `if isinstance(data, dict) or data is not None:` is a tautology equivalent to `if data is not None:` (a dict is never None). So the intended '200-but-unparseable is a server-side oddity; treat as transient' path (lines 1017-1025) is unreachable: resp.json() that parses to None (literal 'null'), a bare JSON string, number, or list is returned as the payload. Any downstream `data.get(...)` (e.g. _query_diag at line 1716) then crashes with AttributeError/TypeError on a non-dict 'successful' response.
all_defects.suggestion: Use `if isinstance(data, dict):` so non-dict/None 200 bodies fall through to the retry/raise path as the comment intends.

all_defects.description: `if fallback and resp.status_code != 200 and (retryable or not fast_fail and fallback is not None):` — `and` binds tighter than `or`, so the condition is `... and (retryable or ((not fast_fail) and (fallback is not None)))`. `fallback is not None` is always true here (first clause of the chain), making the inner `and` dead; and a fast-fail status that is also retryable (e.g. a 429 body tagged component=authentication) silently takes the fallback, inverting the 'definitive errors are not retried/fallen-back' contract stated in the docstring (lines 975-976).
all_defects.suggestion: Explicitly parenthesise: `if fallback and resp.status_code != 200 and (retryable or not fast_fail):` and drop the redundant `fallback is not None` (and possibly the _fallback_ok stub).

all_defects.description: In the default call (max_age_hours=None), `fetch([result_r.url], max_characters=text_cap, include_sections=["body"], text_verbosity="standard", max_age_hours=None)` hits fetch()'s backward-compat single-URL string branch (fetch lines 1823-1832: condition `len(results)==1 and mode=="text" and not(with_highlights or with_summary) and not extras_links and max_age_hours is None` is all True, and it does not account for include_sections/text_verbosity). So `body` is a `str`, not a list. The `isinstance(body, list)` check at line 4456 is then False, so website_url/website_title/website_text are NEVER added, and no website_error is set either. The docstring promises these fields on a successful fetch_website, but the normal success path returns a dict without them.
all_defects.suggestion: Pass include_meta=True (fetch then returns an envelope with 'results'), or force a non-None max_age_hours, or make fetch() treat include_sections/text_verbosity as 'rich options' that disable the string form. Then read body['results'][0]['text'].

all_defects.description: The deprecation gate regex r"\b(deprecat|obsolete|removed|migrat|breaking|sunset)\b" (also 5800, and the shaded copies 5550/5554/5567) requires a word boundary on BOTH sides of each stem. Since 'deprecat', 'remov', 'migrat' are stems, not whole words, \bdeprecat\b only matches the literal non-word 'deprecat'. Verified: it fails to match 'deprecated', 'deprecation', 'deprecating', 'removed', 'removal', 'migration', 'migrating' — i.e. the actual deprecation vocabulary — while only catching whole words 'obsolete', 'removed', 'breaking', 'sunset', 'end of life'. _dep_type() (substring, no \b) would classify 'deprecated' fine, but items never reach it because this gate rejects them first. Net effect: deprecations() returns near-empty signals/counts for its primary use case.
all_defects.suggestion: Drop the trailing \b (keep leading \b only) or use substring matching: r"\b(deprecat|obsolet|end[- ]of[- ]life|remov|migrat|breaking|sunset)" so stems match as prefixes.

all_defects.description: _get_api_key returns _API_KEY_CACHE[label] before ever re-reading the environment.
