Passing stream=True to answer() crashes with an obscure error; the documented streaming path is stream_answer().
all_defects.suggestion: Either document/validate stream (raise a clear error directing the user to stream_answer when stream=True) or parse the SSE stream; simplest is to reject stream=True with an ExaError pointing to stream_answer().

all_defects.description: The legacy string-form guard checks only `not extras_links and max_age_hours is None` (line 1824), ignoring the other rich extras (extras_image_links, extras_rich_links, extras_rich_image_links, extras_code_blocks) and other rich options (text_verbosity, subpages, include_sections, highlights_max_characters). So a single-URL text fetch such as fetch(urls=[u], extras_code_blocks=5) still returns the plain '--- Title ---\n<body>' string and silently discards the requested structured extras, contradicting the docstring promise that the string form is used only 'when no rich options are requested'.
all_defects.suggestion: Make the guard cover all rich options (any extras_*, text_verbosity, subpages>0, subpage_target, include_sections, etc.) so the structured list is returned whenever a rich option is actually requested.

all_defects.description: Answer.__init__ sets self.citations = raw.get("citations", []) (line 1854). If the /answer API returns the key with a null value ("citations": null) the default is not applied, so citations becomes None; Answer.sources (line 1860), to_dict (line 1866), to_markdown (line 1879) and __repr__ (line 1891) then raise TypeError ('NoneType' not iterable / not a len()). The sibling stream_answer defensively normalizes with `obj.get("citations") or []` (line 2672), confirming empty/absent citations is a real response shape, so Answer should use the same guard.
all_defects.suggestion: Use self.citations = raw.get("citations") or [] to mirror stream_answer and avoid the None crash.

all_defects.description: agent() early-returns a terminal run created already terminal (`if run.done: return run`) without running the `raise_on_failed` check at line 2425. If POST /agent/runs returns a run that is already `failed` (rare per the comment, but e.g. an instantly-failing continuation), the default `raise_on_failed=True` contract documented in the docstring (lines 2368-2369, 2375-2377) is violated: a failed AgentRun is silently returned instead of raising ExaError, unlike the poll path which does raise.
all_defects.suggestion: Move/apply the `if raise_on_failed and run.status == "failed": raise` check after the early return as well (check both the pre-poll and post-poll run objects).

all_defects.description: The docstring says `timeout` is the 'Max total wall-clock seconds to wait for completion' (line 2366), but `deadline = time.time() + timeout` is computed AFTER the create call at line 2404, which itself runs with `timeout=min(timeout, 30)`; each in-flight poll GET at line 2412 also carries `timeout=min(timeout, 45)`. Total elapsed wall-clock can therefore exceed `timeout` by up to ~30s (create) + up to ~45s (one in-flight poll) for default timeout=120, and for small timeouts (e.g. timeout=10) the actual wait can be roughly double the promised bound.
all_defects.suggestion: Subtract elapsed time from the create call before computing the deadline (e.g. record t0 before POST and use `deadline = t0 + timeout`), and/or cap the per-poll request timeout by remaining time.

all_defects.description: fast_fail treats VALIDATION as definitive only when `resp.status_code == 422 and code == 'VALIDATION'`, whereas _classify_response (line 857) classifies `code == 'VALIDATION'` as 'param' regardless of status. A 400/500 response whose body carries error.code='VALIDATION' therefore gets retried by _request (fast_fail False) and, after retries, raised with category='param' even though the real failure was a non-validation HTTP error — callers reacting on .category get the wrong verdict.
all_defects.suggestion: Align the two: have _request compute fast_fail via the same predicate as _classify_response, or drop the status guard in _classify_response.

all_defects.description: In _classify_response, if the meta.errors normalisation comprehension raises (e.g. an entry whose 'loc' is a non-iterable non-string), `except Exception: pass` leaves `details` as the RAW unnormalized list (still set from line 859). The caller then reports un-normalised details and str()s the raw list in the 200-char message instead of falling back to the body text.
all_defects.suggestion: Set `details = None` (or a sentinel) in the except block so the fallback message uses the raw body.

all_defects.description: _read_key_file accepts ANY line with length >= 12 and no '/' as the API key (`elif len(line) >= 12 and "/" not in line and line not in names: return line...`). For a file like ~/.prime/agent/keys/secrets.env that also defines BRAVE_API_KEY, the first 12+ char line that isn't KEY=VALUE for a Brave name (a comment without '#', a shebang, another service's bare token) is returned as the Brave key before the real BRAVE_API_KEY= line is ever seen — wrong credential silently used.
all_defects.suggestion: Only return bare-line values from files dedicated to this key (the stem.key / names.lower().key files); require KEY=VALUE form for generic .env files.

all_defects.description: top_terms() docstring (lines 1007-1008) promises domain_clusters entries shaped {"domain","results"} but the actual key returned is "count" ({"domain": d, "count": c}). Downstream code or skill instructions following the documented shape get KeyError on 'results'.
all_defects.suggestion: Either rename the returned key to 'results' or fix the docstring to 'count'.

all_defects.description: entity_schema() silently coerces any unsupported entity kind that HAS properties to typ='company' (line 931). For a record with type 'entity' or 'organization' (both are real Exa kinds; 'entity' is even in the _ENTITY_TYPES tuple) it returns type='company', schema_model='CompanyEntity', and presence/absence computed against company fields - the returned 'type' no longer matches entity_type(entity), mislabeling the entity and its missing/present lists.
all_defects.suggestion: Return the original kind in 'type' and report the known-attribute surface for an unrecognized kind instead of forcing the company schema (or add an explicit 'coerced_from' field).

all_defects.description: entity_search() accepts dedupe: bool = True but never reads it; deduplication always happens, so dedupe=False still dedupes - a silent contract violation for callers who pass it.
all_defects.suggestion: Honor dedupe=False (skip roster dedup, keep all records) or drop the parameter.

all_defects.description: monitor_create's `timeout=45.0` keyword is accepted (line 2934) but never used; the request hardcodes timeout=30. A caller passing timeout=120 gets a 30s request that can raise httpx.TimeoutException earlier than requested, and the default is also not the documented 45s.
all_defects.suggestion: Pass timeout=timeout to _request (or drop the parameter).

all_defects.description: monitor_check docstring promises a dict with 'latest_run' (and references nonexistent parameter 'auto_if_empty' at line 3114); the actual returns are {monitor_id, has_run, run_id, run_output, triggered} with no 'latest_run' key in either branch (lines 3123-3129, 3135-3141). Callers keying off documented fields get KeyError/None.
all_defects.suggestion: Add 'latest_run' (the full run dict) to both return dicts or fix the docstring; rename auto_if_empty to trigger_if_empty.

all_defects.description: monitor_check triggers a new run whenever runs_data[0] has no output, even when an older completed run with output exists, and even while a run is in progress. Docstring (line 3103) and jobs.md say it should only trigger when the monitor has NO completed run, so e.g. runs=[running, completed-with-output] triggers a duplicate/paid run contrary to documented semantics.
all_defects.suggestion: Scan the fetched runs for a completed run with output first; only trigger if none exists (and ideally skip if latest is still 'running').

all_defects.description: webset_eval_review's docstring (lines 3668-3669) promises keys 'item_count' and 'by_satisfied', but the actual return (lines 3697-3698) uses 'count' and 'by_satisfaction'. Any caller following the documented shape gets KeyError on result['item_count'] or result['by_satisfied'].
all_defects.suggestion: Rename the returned keys to match the docstring (item_count, by_satisfied) or update the docstring to 'count'/'by_satisfaction'.

all_defects.description: is_deprecated() derives its entire 'deprecated' verdict from deprecations(...).get('signals') (line 5915-5917). Because deprecations() is neutered by the broken \b regex gate, signals is almost always empty, so is_deprecated() returns {'deprecated': False} even for genuinely deprecated packages. The freshness/news check (active_recent) does not feed the verdict, so the advertised deprecation-detection capability silently does not work.
all_defects.suggestion: Fix the regex gate in deprecations() (root cause); optionally add a direct deprecation-keyword search in is_deprecated() so the verdict is not single-sourced to one fragile classifier.

all_defects.description: Five functions are defined twice in this range; the first definition of each is shadowed and never executed at runtime (module dict keeps the last binding). Pairs: pkg_releases 5459->5705, _dep_type 5507->5753, deprecations 5522->5768, snippet 5581->5826, code_lint_tips 5672->5870. The 5459/5507/5522/5581/5672 copies (plus the duplicated banner comment at 5450-5456 and 5696-5702) are dead. This is ~200 lines of duplicated code and a maintenance hazard (any future edit must be applied to two places).
all_defects.suggestion: Delete the first (shaded) copies at 5459, 5507, 5522, 5581, 5672 and the duplicate banner comment at 5450-5456, keeping only the effective 5705/5753/5768/5826/5870 block and the single banner.

all_defects.description: The ThreadPoolExecutor is a process-lifetime singleton sized by the FIRST call to _pool/_fanout. A later _fanout(jobs, concurrency=N) with N > the initial size silently runs on the smaller pool, and max(8, ...) forces at least 8 in-flight jobs even when the caller explicitly passes a smaller concurrency (e.g. concurrency=2 to stay under a rate limit still submits with 8 running). The `concurrency` parameter therefore does not reliably bound parallelism.
all_defects.suggestion: Create/resize the pool when requested max_workers exceeds the current pool size (or document that the first call's concurrency is fixed for the process and honor a lower bound instead of max(8, ...)).

all_defects.description: Missing key raises a bare RuntimeError, but the ExaAuthError docstring (lines 382-383) says it covers 'the API key is missing, invalid, or revoked' and references/usage.md tells users to catch ExaAuthError for auth problems. Callers following the docs and catching ExaAuthError will miss the missing-key case entirely.
all_defects.suggestion: Raise ExaAuthError (or document RuntimeError explicitly) for the not-configured case so the documented catch set works.

all_defects.description: _read_key_file's bare-token branch returns the first line with no '=', length >= 12 and no '/' as the key without checking it belongs to any name in `names`. In a key/env file whose first qualifying token is not the Exa key (e.g. a comment-free header token, a date-like string, or another service's token in secrets.env), the wrong value is silently returned as the API key, surfacing later only as a confusing 401.
all_defects.suggestion: For files that contain '='-style lines, require NAME= matches; only accept a bare token when the file contains no assignment lines at all (or name it <stem>.key explicitly).

all_defects.description: stream_answer's docstring documents the trailing meta dict as "cost_dollars": {...} (an object), and the rest of the module treats cost as a dict (e.g. costDollars.total, SearchResults.total_cost). But the code (line 2675) collapses it to the scalar float (obj.get('costDollars') or {}).get('total'), so the yielded dict actually carries cost_dollars as a float/None.
all_defects.suggestion: Either emit the raw costDollars dict to match the doc/module convention, or fix the docstring example to show a scalar; a caller that does meta['cost_dollars']['total'] per the documented shape raises TypeError/AttributeError.

all_defects.description: stream_search builds body['numResults']=num_results with no client-side validation. search() calls _validate_search_params (line 1488) to enforce 1<=num_results<=100, and references/usage.md (line 32) advertises that 'the client validates num_results from 1-100'. stream_search skips this, so num_results=0/200 reach the API and surface as a raw HTTP 400 wrapped in a generic ExaError rather than the clear client-side ExaError the sibling path gives.
all_defects.suggestion: Call _validate_search_params (or at least range-check num_results) before opening the stream to match search() behavior and the documented client-side validation.

all_defects.description: Key `"megabyte-kilobybyte"` is a typo for `"megabyte-kilobyte"`. A MB-to-KB conversion via `_convert_unit` looks up `"megabyte-kilobyte"` (correctly spelled, lowercased at line 3924) which is not in the dict, so `_UNITCONV_FACTORS.get(key)` returns None and `_rich_unitconv` returns `result=None` instead of the expected value (e.g. 1024 for 1 MB).
all_defects.suggestion: Rename the key to `"megabyte-kilobyte"`.

all_defects.description: `d.get("pronounciation")` uses a misspelled key. If the Brave API returns the correctly-spelled key `"pronunciation"`, the `pronunciation` field in the normalised output will always be None. The docstring for `_rich_definitions` lists `pronunciation` as a returned field.
all_defects.suggestion: Change to `d.get("pronunciation")` (or use a fallback: `d.get("pronunciation") or d.get("pronounciation")`) after verifying the actual API response key.

all_defects.description: `h.split()[0]` raises IndexError when `h` is an empty string ("".split() returns [], and [0] on an empty list crashes). The `isinstance(h, str)` guard at line 3487 passes for "", so the second half of the `and` is evaluated and crashes. A venue row whose `opening_hours` list contains an empty string would crash `open_now` with IndexError instead of returning a graceful result.
all_defects.suggestion: Guard with `if isinstance(h, str) and h and h.split()[0].startswith(day[:3]):` or use `parts = h.split(); if parts and parts[0].startswith(day[:3]):`.

all_defects.description: rich() docstring (lines 4073-4074) promises the package always contains "render" and "raw", but the early-return path at lines 4085-4087 (no callback_key, or fetch=False) omits both keys. SKILL.md/verticals.md say no-hint is a normal outcome, so consumers doing out["raw"] or out["render"] on a hintless query raise KeyError. Two return shapes for one function.
all_defects.suggestion: Always include "render" (empty string) and "raw" ({}) in the early return, or document that the keys are absent on the hint-only path.

all_defects.description: The typed helpers weather/stock_quote/crypto/definition/currency_x/convert_values (lines 4220-4251) blindly return rich() output without checking that the hint's vertical actually matches the requested subtype. Their docstrings promise results[0]["data"] is the specific normalised block, but if the hint maps to a different vertical (e.g. stock_quote("apple") returning a definitions vertical) or returns no hint at all, callers silently get wrong-vertical or empty data with no warning.
all_defects.suggestion: In each helper, compare result["vertical"] (or results[0]["subtype"]) to the expected subtype and either return a flagged/empty package or at least note the mismatch.

all_defects.description: In drinks(), `dom = (r.get("domain") or "").lower()` reads a `domain` key off the web result item `r`. Web items are normalized by _web_item (line 1283) which has NO `domain` key (its site field is `site`), so r.get("domain") is always None and dom is always "". The domain-based drink heuristic `any(s in dom for s in ("liquor","cocktail","drink","wine"))` therefore never fires, contrary to the documented intent (docstring lines 3201-3203: "whose title/domain signals a cocktail"). Drink recipes that would otherwise be caught via their source host are silently dropped, yielding an under-sized results set.
all_defects.suggestion: Use the web item's site host `r.get("site")` (or the recipe block's domain `rc.get("domain")` if that is what was meant) instead of the nonexistent `r.get("domain")`.

all_defects.description: In structured(), each discussions entry is built as {"title": d.get("title"), "url": d.get("url"), "site": _host(d), "forum": d.get("forum")}. `data.get("discussions")` holds NORMALIZED discussion items from _discussion_item (line 1497), which already carry a `site` field and do NOT carry `meta_url`. _host() (line 1081) reads item.get("meta_url") and returns None when absent, so `_host(d)` is always None. Consequently the `site` key in every structured()["discussions"] entry is always None.
all_defects.suggestion: Use `d.get("site")` (the pre-normalized host) instead of `_host(d)`.

all_defects.description: software()'s docstring (line 2381) documents the return key as `"registries":{pypi->[names], npm->[names]}`, but the actual returned dict uses the key `"registry"` (line 2419). A caller following the documented contract does res["registries"] and gets KeyError. Relatedly, the docstring says `versions` is `[version str...]` while the code returns a list of dicts {name,version,url,code} (line 2398).
all_defects.suggestion: Rename the returned key to `registries` to match the docstring, or correct the docstring to `registry`; also fix the `versions` doc description to list-of-dicts.

all_defects.description: research() computes 'duplicates' as sum(p['n'] for p in per_search if p['n']) - len(out_items). Each per-query 'n' equals the count of items actually appended to out_items for that query, so the sum always equals len(out_items) and 'duplicates' is always 0. It never reflects the URLs actually dropped during cross-query dedup (the value the docstring 'duplicates: int' implies).
all_defects.suggestion: Track the raw pre-dedup count per query and subtract the kept count, or compute duplicates from a seen-set hit counter rather than the appended count.

all_defects.description: For mode='all', web-only params discussion_count/video_count/movie_count are added to the shared 'params' dict (lines 1940-1945) and then spread into every fanout sub-request via {**params, ...} (lines 1982-1986). Passing e.g. video_count=3 with mode='all' sends it to /res/v1/news/search and /res/v1/videos/search, which do not accept it -> likely HTTP 422 VALIDATION, failing the whole 'all' composite. text_decorations leaks the same way.
all_defects.suggestion: Build separate per-endpoint param dicts for the 'all' fanout, or strip web-only keys (discussion_count/video_count/movie_count/text_decorations) from the news and video sub-requests.

all_defects.description: local mode sets fallback=PATHS['web'] and documents 'falls back to web' (mode doc line 742, comment line 2058-2059), but the fallback only fires in _request when the failure is retryable (429/5xx) or a non-fast_fail 4xx. A 401/403 from /res/v1/local/search is classified fast_fail, so _request raises (line 1045-1046) and never runs the web fallback. The most likely 'key lacks local access' case therefore does NOT fall back to web.
all_defects.suggestion: In _request, run the fallback before raising on fast_fail when a fallback path is supplied, or special-case local->web so 401/403 also triggers the web fallback.

all_defects.description: _fanout's `concurrency` argument does not control actual in-flight concurrency. It only feeds `_pool(max(8, concurrency))`, and _pool creates the executor exactly once (first call wins); _WORKERS is never resized. So the pool's worker count is fixed by whichever call first touched it (typically the 8-worker default), and every later _fanout(concurrency=2/3/4/16) silently reuses that same pool. The documented `batch(concurrency=...)` 'max in-flight requests' knob and the mode-specific limits (mosaic=3, rich=2, paged=4) are effectively no-ops: all jobs queue to the same fixed-size pool.
all_defects.suggestion: Create a dedicated bounded executor per concurrency value, or use a semaphore to actually cap in-flight jobs, or drop the parameter so it isn't misleading.

all_defects.description: _norm_url lowercases the ENTIRE URL (scheme+host+path+query) and returns u.lower(). URL paths and query values are case-sensitive per RFC 3986, so two distinct results whose paths differ only by case (e.g. /Page vs /page, /Apple vs /apple) are treated as the same identity. This silently drops legitimately-distinct hits in _dedupe_hits and can over-suppress the image/page/website 'same URL' checks in _slim_item/_slim_infobox.
all_defects.suggestion: Lowercase only the scheme and host; preserve case in the path and query string.

all_defects.description: For a timestamped date, _one_date returns `s.replace("Z", "").split(".")[0]`, stripping the trailing 'Z' (UTC marker). The resulting string (e.g. '2025-01-15T10:30:00') is a naive ISO string with no timezone; consumers that parse it (Python <=3.10 fromisoformat, or downstream code) treat it as wall-clock/local time, shifting the real UTC instant by the viewer's offset. The stripping appears aimed at py3.10 fromisoformat not accepting 'Z', but it silently discards timezone information from the 'date' field the agent view exposes.
all_defects.suggestion: Preserve the timezone (e.g. keep 'Z' or convert to an explicit offset) rather than emitting a naive string, or document that 'date' is UTC-naive.

all_defects.description: search(stream=True) sets body['stream']=True, but the transport _request() always parses a single JSON body via resp.json() (line 510) and never consumes an SSE stream. The parameter is therefore a no-op that cannot deliver a stream; the real streaming path is the separate stream_search() at line 2807. Advertsing `stream` on search() is misleading.
all_defects.suggestion: Remove the `stream` parameter from search() or route it to the streaming transport; it currently cannot work.

all_defects.description: In _contents_block, include_html_tags, include_sections and exclude_sections are emitted only inside the text sub-dict (lines 1360-1365), which is only reached when `with_text or max_characters or text_verbosity` is truthy. If a caller sets only e.g. include_sections=[...] with no text option, the entire block is skipped and the parameter is silently ignored with no error.
all_defects.suggestion: Either reject these section/HTML options when no text is requested, or at least warn; don't silently drop them.

all_defects.description: livecrawl is annotated Optional[str] in search() (and defaults to False in _contents_block at line 1340), but the Exa contents field is a boolean and is emitted verbatim via `if livecrawl: c['livecrawl'] = livecrawl` (line 1405). Passing a string would send a string where the API expects a bool.
all_defects.suggestion: Type it as Optional[bool] and normalize to bool before emitting.

all_defects.description: _category_canon prints a warning to stdout and returns None for an unsupported category, so the user's requested category filter is silently not applied and search() runs without it. For a library this means stdout output on a data path and results that differ from what was requested, with no exception.
all_defects.suggestion: Consider raising or returning a sentinel that lets search() decide; stdout-print from a helper is a code smell and the filter drop is easy to miss.

all_defects.description: Several normalizers do x = item.get(field) or {} and then call .get() on it with only a truthiness guard, so a truthy non-dict value (e.g. a string) causes AttributeError. _web_item: free_flag = article.get(...) at line 1305 (every other article access at lines 1285/1287/1335 is isinstance-guarded), org.get('name') at line 1349, thumb.get at lines 1353-1355, profile.get at lines 1358-1361. Same pattern in _news_item line 1482 (prof.get), _discussion_item lines 1498/1505/1511 (d.get on item.data), and _recipe_item/_product_item/_movie_item thumbnail access (lines 1203-1204, 1240-1241, 1278-1279).
all_defects.suggestion: Apply the file's standard isinstance(x, dict) guard (as done for creative_work, embedded_video, and opening_hours at line 1607/1619) before calling .get.

all_defects.description: _infobox does b = ib[0] without checking that the first infobox result is a dict; a non-dict entry makes b.get('title') at line 1689 raise AttributeError. Note _loc_lines (line 1680) filters its items with isinstance(i, dict) but _infobox does not; a non-dict data['infobox'] value also crashes at line 1684 on .get('results').
all_defects.suggestion: Guard with isinstance(ib[0], dict) (return None otherwise) and isinstance(data.get('infobox'), dict).

all_defects.description: _infobox silently truncates long_desc to 800 characters (_clean_html(...)[:800]). The skill docs (api.md 'Return shapes', verticals.md) describe the full view as carrying normalized detailed fields without mentioning this cap, so consumers see 'long_desc' that may be cut mid-sentence with no indicator that it was truncated.
all_defects.suggestion: Either document the 800-char cap in SKILL.md/references, or add a 'long_desc_truncated' flag to the returned dict.

all_defects.description: Answer.to_markdown renders the answer body with str(self.answer) (line 1877). When output_schema is supplied, self.answer is a dict, and str() emits Python repr (single-quoted, non-JSON) rather than valid JSON, so the '## Answer' block is not a clean structured payload.
all_defects.suggestion: Serialize a dict answer with json.dumps(answer, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) instead of str() when the answer is not a string.

all_defects.description: agent_trace() wraps json.loads of a string event `data` in `try/except: pass` (lines 2317-2321), so if the API ever returns a string payload that is not valid JSON the field stays a str. AgentTrace._parse then calls `data.get(...)` on that str (e.g. line 2129 `item = data.get("item") or {}`), raising AttributeError 'str' object has no attribute 'get' and crashing agent_trace entirely.
all_defects.suggestion: On parse failure, drop the event or set e["data"] = {} instead of leaving the raw string, or make AgentTrace._parse tolerate non-dict `data` (guard with isinstance(d, dict)).

all_defects.description: AgentRun.citations iterates `for c in g.get("citations", [])`; the default only covers a missing key. If the API sends a grounding group with `"citations": null`, iterating None raises TypeError. The sibling code in this file consistently defends with `or []` (e.g. AgentRun.__init__ line 1967, AgentTrace._parse lines 2129/2142), so a null here is handled less defensively than the rest of the module.
all_defects.suggestion: Use `for c in (g.get("citations") or []):`.

all_defects.description: `elif code == "VALIDATION" or status == 422 and meta.get("errors"):` parses as `code == 'VALIDATION' or (status == 422 and meta.get('errors'))` due to precedence; works by luck but any 4xx/5xx body containing error.code='VALIDATION' is classified 'param' with meta.errors possibly empty/None, even though the transport error is the real issue. Add parentheses for clarity.
all_defects.suggestion: elif code == "VALIDATION" or (status == 422 and meta.get("errors")):

all_defects.description: `try: from dotenv import dotenv_values ... except Exception: pass` wraps the entire dotenv loop, but only an ImportError can occur before the loop body; any unexpected error from dotenv_values() (corrupt/oversized .env) is silently swallowed, so a misconfigured dotenv file yields no signal and the search later fails with the generic 'no API key' message.
all_defects.suggestion: Catch only ImportError around the import; let dotenv_values errors surface or log them.

all_defects.description: BraveError docstring lists `timeout` and `http_422` as valid categories, but grep confirms neither string is ever assigned anywhere in the module. Callers checking `category == 'timeout'` (or distinguishing http_422 from param) can never match; timeouts surface as category='network' instead.
all_defects.suggestion: Either assign these categories where timeouts/422s are handled, or remove them from the docstring.

all_defects.description: The `timeout` parameter of _classify_response is never referenced in the body; it is threaded from _request (lines 1046/1047) purely for symmetry.
all_defects.suggestion: Drop the parameter or use it in the message (e.g. note the timeout value on network-related classifications).

all_defects.description: The error message embeds `str(details if details else body)[:200]` — up to 200 chars of the raw response body (or raw details list repr) into an exception message. If a response body ever echoes the X-Subscription-Token or other credential material, it would leak into logs/agent transcripts.
all_defects.suggestion: Limit the embedded body to a fixed set of safe fields (error.code/error.detail) rather than raw body text.

all_defects.description: _fallback_ok is a trivial `return bool(fallback)` stub invoked only from _request line 1042 where the enclosing `if fallback and ...` already guarantees truthiness; it adds an indirection with no decision.
all_defects.suggestion: Inline the check (or remove both) and let _request call _run_fallback directly.

all_defects.description: _get_api_key backfills the resolved key into os.environ for ALL _API_KEY_NAMES via setdefault — a side effect beyond the documented lookup, mutating process-wide state for sibling threads/imports and non-thread-safe with concurrent first calls (two threads can both miss the cache and race the setdefault; harmless result-wise since values agree, but the env mutation is observable).
all_defects.suggestion: Document the env backfill explicitly or drop it; guard the cache read/write if true concurrency on first use is expected.

all_defects.description:
In _clean_html, line 796's html.unescape already converts ' ' to U+00A0, so the `re.sub(r" ", " ", t)` at line 800 can never match; and line 803 `re.sub(r"\s*
\s*", "
", ...)` is a no-op that keeps the space on each side of a newline, so 'a
   b' collapses to 'a 
 b' rather than a clean line break (minor cosmetic noise in readable output).
all_defects.suggestion: Delete line 800 and use `re.sub(r"[ \t]*\n[ \t]*", "\n", t)` if strict line breaks are wanted.

all_defects.description: entity_search() wraps entity_summary() in 'except Exception: continue' with no log; malformed entity records (e.g. a non-dict entry in entities[]) are dropped silently, so the roster can quietly lose entities and entity_count is under-reported with no trace.
all_defects.suggestion: Narrow to (AttributeError, TypeError), or count skipped records and surface it in the result dict.

all_defects.description: _occurrences counts entity records, not distinct source pages: if one result carries two records that share a dedupe key (no library id, same name+type), a single page inflates the count to 2, contradicting the docstrings 'how many distinct result pages mentioned each entity' / 'number of source pages that surfaced it'.
all_defects.suggestion: Count per-result distinctness (e.g. add one per Result that contains the key) or reword the docstring to 'occurrences'.

all_defects.description: entity_schema() discovery check 'if typ in ("unknown", "") and not props:' - the '' branch is unreachable: entity_type() always returns at least 'unknown' (str(t or 'unknown')), never an empty string.
all_defects.suggestion: Simplify to 'if typ == "unknown" and not props:'.

all_defects.description: _ENTITY_TYPES is defined but never referenced anywhere in the module (grep-verified); it is also not part of __all__.
all_defects.suggestion: Use it (e.g. as the set of known kinds in entity_schema) or delete it.

all_defects.description: Result.domain (line 691) and Result.hostname (line 696) fall back to self.id when url is empty; Exa result ids are opaque hex strings, not URLs, so _domain_of() returns the whole id as a fake 'domain' (e.g. 'a3f9...') that then pollutes SearchResults.domains()/top_domains() and top_terms() domain_clusters.
all_defects.suggestion: Return '' when url is missing instead of feeding the id through _domain_of.

all_defects.description: SearchResults.to_agent() uses 'if cost:' so a legitimate cost of 0.0 (free/zero-cost request) is omitted from the output, while __repr__ and total_cost() treat 0.0 as a real value - inconsistent handling.
all_defects.suggestion: Use 'if cost is not None:'.

all_defects.description: Result.to_agent() only date-truncates when the time part startswith '00:00:00'; midnight timestamps with a shorter or fractional time (e.g. '2024-01-01T00:00' or '2024-01-01T00:00.000Z') keep the time part, violating the docstring promise 'Date keeps time when it is not midnight'.
all_defects.suggestion: Compare the parsed time portion (e.g. hour/minute/second all zero) rather than string prefix.

all_defects.description: Module constants _CADENCE and _BEHAVIOR (lines 3092-3093) are defined but never referenced anywhere in the file; wmonitor_create/wmonitor_update use the literals 'cadence'/'behavior' inline.
all_defects.suggestion: Remove them or use them in wmonitor_create/wmonitor_update.

all_defects.description: monitor_wait treats 'failed'/'cancelled' as terminal success and just returns the run dict; jobs.md explicitly notes 'a terminal failed/cancelled state is not success' but the API gives callers no signal beyond manually checking status (contrast agent() which raises via raise_on_failed). The timeout error also renders as 'monitor run None did not finish' when run_id is None (line 3056).
all_defects.suggestion: Return or raise distinctly for failed/cancelled, or document that callers must inspect run['status']; use monitor_id in the timeout message when run_id is None.

all_defects.description: monitor_create does a local `import time` that is both redundant (time is imported at module scope, line 12) and unused in the function body.
all_defects.suggestion: Delete the local import.

all_defects.description: monitor_create docstring says 'num_results: result count per run (default API 10)' but the client default is num_results=5 (line 2923), so every call that omits it sends 5, not the API default.
all_defects.suggestion: Fix the docstring to state the client default of 5.

all_defects.description: wmonitor_create computes timeout=min(timeout, 30) with default timeout=45.0, so the effective HTTP timeout is always 30s and any caller-supplied value above 30 is silently reduced; the docstring does not document this cap.
all_defects.suggestion: Pass timeout through unchanged or document the 30s cap.

all_defects.description: `nrows = sum(1 for _ in fh)` counts every line of the CSV including the header row, and this is sent as the `count` body field (line 3944). If the API's `count` is expected to be the number of entity records, it is off by one (and by more if the file has a trailing empty line).
all_defects.suggestion: Subtract the header line (and any blank lines) so `count` reflects record count, e.g. count data rows only.

all_defects.description: In the dedupe path, results lacking both url and id are silently dropped (`u = _canon(...)`; `if not u: continue`), so such results never appear in the merged SearchResults. merge_searches (line 4277-4281) preserves them in `extra_results` instead. The two functions handle the same no-URL case inconsistently.
all_defects.suggestion: Preserve no-URL results (append after the URL-deduped ones, as merge_searches does) rather than dropping them.

all_defects.description: `return search_results[0] if isinstance(search_results[0], SearchResults) else search_results[0]` has two identical branches, so the ternary is a no-op. Also the documented 'returned unchanged (fast path)' for a single input only applies when dedupe=True; with dedupe=False and one input it falls through to a full merge that re-indexes and returns a new SearchResults.
all_defects.suggestion: Simplify to `return search_results[0]` and clarify the docstring that the unchanged fast path is only for dedupe=True.

all_defects.description: event_list sends the same event-type filter twice: a singular `type` param (line 4068) AND a plural `types` list into which event_type is also re-appended (lines 4072-4074). When event_type is given, its value is thus present in both query params, which is redundant and risks the API double-applying or rejecting the combined filter.
all_defects.suggestion: Pick one representation: either set `type` only when event_type is the sole filter, or rely solely on `types` and drop the singular `type` param.

all_defects.description: webset_eval_review declares timeout=45.0 but never uses it; the only API call is webset_items(webset_id, limit=limit, cursor=cursor), which does not accept a timeout. The param is silently ignored.
all_defects.suggestion: Remove the unused timeout param or plumb a timeout into webset_items/_request.

all_defects.description: webset_recall declares timeout=45.0 but never uses it; its two API calls, webset_get(webset_id) and webset_search_status(webset_id, search_id), take no timeout argument. The param is silently ignored.
all_defects.suggestion: Remove the unused timeout param or add timeout support to the underlying helpers.

all_defects.description: webset_wait's non-search_id branch returns immediately when 'not searches' (empty list). For a freshly created webset whose searches array is transiently empty, this returns before any search has been registered, so the wait effectively no-ops instead of polling to terminal.
all_defects.suggestion: Only treat an empty searches list as terminal when the webset status is paused/cancelled/failed; otherwise keep polling.

all_defects.description: webset_items_all uses a 'while True' that keeps appending to 'items' and advancing cursor until hasMore is false. There is no duplicate-page / progress guard: if the API ever repeats a cursor or keeps hasMore true, the loop is infinite and the list grows without bound. Same class of risk applies to webset_snapshot which holds the full list in memory.
all_defects.suggestion: Add a safety bound (max pages, or stop when a nextCursor repeats) to prevent infinite pagination.

all_defects.description: In enrichment_update (and webset_update/webset_enrich), description/format/options are guarded by truthiness ('if description:') while metadata uses 'is not None'. A caller passing empty string '' or None to clear description/format silently omits it from the PATCH body, so it cannot be cleared, unlike metadata. Minor and likely intentional, but inconsistent within the same call.
all_defects.suggestion: If clearing fields is a supported use case, gate all fields on 'is not None' rather than truthiness.

all_defects.description: deprecations() docstring promises signals entries of shape {url,title,type,snippet}, but the code only ever builds {url, title, type} — 'snippet' is never populated. Additionally, markdown line 5821 does s.get('url') which is None for the answer-derived signal (url=None at 5801) and null citation urls, so the rendered line prints a literal 'None'.
all_defects.suggestion: Either add a 'snippet' field (e.g. truncated title/url) to each signal dict or correct the docstring; guard the None url in the markdown line (use s.get('url') or '').

all_defects.description: api_reference() docstring states 'max_characters: max text to keep (default 16000)' but the signature default is 9000 (line 5625). The actual capped text passed to fetch() is 9000.
all_defects.suggestion: Correct the docstring default to 9000 (or change the signature default to 16000 if that was intended).

all_defects.description: deprecations() uses datetime.utcnow() (both copies: 5558 and 5803), which is deprecated in Python 3.12+ (emits DeprecationWarning). The value is only used for a date-string window, so it is not a correctness bug, but it is inconsistent with the rest of the module which uses datetime.now(timezone.utc) (e.g. 3581, 4347).
all_defects.suggestion: Replace datetime.utcnow() with datetime.now(timezone.utc) to match the module's other date handling.

all_defects.description: hf_discussions() wraps each of its two search() calls in 'except Exception: pass' (5430-5437), silently swallowing all errors including missing/invalid API key or 4xx/5xx; a fully failed call returns an empty threads list indistinguishable from 'no results'. Same silent-swallow pattern in pkg_releases (news sweep) and both deprecations() call blocks.
all_defects.suggestion: At minimum narrow to ExaError and/or log the exception; returning empty-on-error is defensible but currently hides auth/config failures from the caller.

all_defects.description: Only `except Exception` is caught around fut.result() (line 77); a BaseException raised by a job (SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt) propagates out of _fanout, aborting collection of the remaining already-submitted futures and returning no result at all. Also, if a thunk is not callable, pool.submit raises TypeError mid-loop after earlier futures are already queued, leaving them orphaned and no partial results.
all_defects.suggestion: Catch BaseException per future (or validate thunks up front and catch submit errors per job) so one bad job cannot discard the whole fanout.

all_defects.description: _http (lines 33-35) and _pool (lines 44-46) use unsynchronized check-then-set lazy initialization of the module globals _CLIENT/_WORKERS; two threads racing on first use can each construct a client/pool, and the loser is abandoned (its connections never closed promptly). The _http docstring claims the client is thread-safe but the creation path itself is not atomic.
all_defects.suggestion: Guard creation with a module-level lock (or accept the benign race explicitly in the docstring).

all_defects.description: resp.headers is httpx's case-insensitive headers dict, so resp.headers.get("retry-after") (second operand of the `or`) can never find a header the first .get("Retry-After") missed; the second lookup is a no-op fallback that never adds anything.
all_defects.suggestion: Drop the redundant second .get("retry-after") call.

all_defects.description: `import functools as _functools` is never referenced anywhere in the module; _make_async (line 302) and _apply_async_to (line 323) re-import functools inside the function body instead of using the module-level alias.
all_defects.suggestion: Delete the unused module-level alias (or use it in the two functions).

all_defects.description: Bare 'except Exception: pass' around the dotenv import + value loop swallows all errors (unreadable/permission-denied dotenv files, parser bugs) and falls through to key-file lookup with no trace; the fallback chain then returns '' or a wrong-source key without indicating the dotenv step failed.
all_defects.suggestion: Catch only ImportError for the missing optional dependency; let per-file read errors raise or at least be distinguishable.

all_defects.description: 'return resp.json()' on any status < 400 is unguarded: a 2xx response with an empty or non-JSON body raises ValueError/json.JSONDecodeError out of _request, which the module's documented error contract (Exa* subclasses from ExaError) does not cover.
all_defects.suggestion: Wrap resp.json() in try/except and raise a wrapped ExaServerError with the status code and a snippet of resp.text.

all_defects.description: Lines 552-553 ('# unreachable' / final raise) are unreachable for any _retries >= 0: every loop path either returns (<400) or raises. Additionally 'last_resp' (assigned lines 504 and 511) is never read, and 'detail' would be None in the dead fallback message.
all_defects.suggestion: Remove the unreachable fallback and the unused last_resp assignment, or convert _retries to assert max(0, _retries) and use last_resp for the diagnostic.

all_defects.description: Redundant 'import time' inside _request; time is already imported at module level (line 12) and used by _retry_after_seconds at module scope.
all_defects.suggestion: Drop the local import.

all_defects.description: __version__ = '0.19.0' is stale: pyproject.toml declares version = '0.20.0' (and the package was imported as v0.20.0 in commit d5e521f), so programmatic version checks disagree with the installed/packaged version.
all_defects.suggestion: Bump to '0.20.0' or read the version from importlib.metadata.

all_defects.description: stream_search (and stream_answer at 2659) parse exactly one JSON object per 'data:' SSE line and, on json failure, `continue` (drop the frame). A valid SSE event whose data value spans multiple 'data:' lines (RFC-allowed) is silently discarded, so a large results/citations frame could vanish. The sibling stream_answer_source handles this correctly with a frame_buffer (2766-2783).
all_defects.suggestion: Buffer consecutive 'data:' lines and join with '\n' before json.loads, as stream_answer_source does, rather than parsing line-by-line.

all_defects.description: stream_search's Yields docstring (2823-2824) lists the final dict as {results, output, grounding, citations, text, request_id}, but the actual final yield (2907-2915) also includes search_time_ms (captured at 2858/2880). The key is undocumented, so a consumer iterating keys or building a schema off the doc misses it.
all_defects.suggestion: Add 'search_time_ms' to the documented final-dict shape.

all_defects.description: pois() builds a `params` dict with a `_idlist` list at lines 4354-4356 that is never used; the actual request uses the `qp` tuple list at line 4357-4368. Misleading dead code next to a comment that already explains the real params mechanism.
all_defects.suggestion: Delete the params/_idlist loop (lines 4354-4356).

all_defects.description: pois() silently truncates ids beyond 20 (lines 4352-4353: id_list = id_list[:20]) and poi_descriptions() does the same (line 4395) with no warning in the returned package; a caller passing 30 ids gets 20 results with n=20 and no indication the rest were dropped.
all_defects.suggestion: Add a field (e.g. "truncated": true or the original count) to the return dict, or raise/annotate when input exceeds the cap.

all_defects.description: _poi_item() guards rating (line 4289-4294), contact (4279-4280), opening_hours.days (4268/4287) with isinstance checks, but reviews/pictures/thumbnail are accessed via bare .get with no dict check: line 4313 (item.get("reviews") or {}).get("results"), 4316 (.get("viewMoreUrl")), 4319 ((item.get("pictures") or {}).get("results")), and 4323-4324 th.get("src"). If any of those fields arrives as a non-dict (list or string), the function crashes with AttributeError mid-normalisation, dropping the whole POI batch in pois().
all_defects.suggestion: Apply the same isinstance-dict guard pattern to reviews, pictures, and thumbnail as is used for rating/contact/days.

all_defects.description: poi_descriptions() render line f"{r.get('title')}: {r.get('description')}" prints the literal string 'None' when title or description is missing, producing 'None: blurb' or 'Title: None' in the readable output instead of omitting the missing part.
all_defects.suggestion: Build the line from the present parts only (e.g. join non-None fields with ': ').

all_defects.description: In research(), when mode is 'news' or 'video', paged() omits web_meta, so for the first query pgm is empty and the code makes a SECOND, redundant _search_full call (line 2316) purely to build web_meta; news/video responses carry no infobox/faq/videos/discussions, so web_meta ends up all-None. Wasteful extra HTTP round-trip on the most common first query.
all_defects.suggestion: Only attempt the meta-fallback _search_full when mode=='web' (the only mode that carries infobox/faq/videos/discussions); skip it for news/video.

all_defects.description: _AsyncBool subclasses int, not bool. isinstance(result, bool) is False and json.dumps serializes it as 1/0 rather than true/false. This only matters if a public function returns a bare bool (none currently do in this section, so it is latent), but it means the 'awaitable bool' is not a real bool to callers using type checks or JSON round-trips.
all_defects.suggestion: Subclass bool, or handle bools by returning a wrapper whose __await__ and JSON behaviour are unambiguous.

all_defects.description: _http() and _pool() use an unsynchronized check-then-set on the module globals _CLIENT/_WORKERS. Under the fanout thread pool the first concurrent use can race and construct two clients / two executors, leaking one. httpx.Client.request is thread-safe, but the lazy init itself is not.
all_defects.suggestion: Guard the one-time init with a module-level lock (or use a module-scope `if _CLIENT is None: _CLIENT = ...` plus a lock / threading.local) so only one instance is created.

all_defects.description: The dual sync/async docstring (lines 511-512) promises that 'the module's own container classes (SearchResults, Answer, ...) get an __await__ that returns the instance unchanged', and _identity_await is defined for exactly that purpose. But no such container class exists in the module (the only classes are the _Async* wrappers and BraveError) and _identity_await is never assigned to any class, so it is dead code and the documented mechanism is not actually present.
all_defects.suggestion: Remove _identity_await and the 'container classes get __await__' claim, or add the container classes if they are intended.
